title: GPU Architecture and Parallel Execution
description: Throughput hardware: grids, SIMT, warps, occupancy, and the schedulers that hide latency. Surprise Me may drop you in this subject; it will not start you on occupancy.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS149 Parallel Computing
sourceReferences.notes: GPU after multi-core and data-parallel thinking.

sourceReferences.title: NVIDIA CUDA C++ Programming Guide
sourceReferences.notes: Thread hierarchy → SIMT/warps → memory → occupancy/divergence as performance.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 6.823
sourceReferences.notes: Vectors/GPUs after pipelining and OOO, not as a first encounter with hardware.

modules.title: GPU execution model
modules.blurb: Why a GPU exists, then grids, SIMT, warps.

modules.title: Resources and the memory hierarchy
modules.blurb: What a warp is competing for, and where data lives.

modules.title: Hiding latency, paying for divergence
modules.blurb: Scheduling interactions — the advanced end of this course.

concepts.name: Why a GPU exists
concepts.summary: Spending transistors on ALUs instead of speculation when the work is wide.
objectives: Contrast a latency-optimized core with a throughput-optimized one
Say what kind of program a GPU is for

concepts.name: Grid, block, thread
concepts.summary: The programmer-visible hierarchy a kernel is launched over.
objectives: Map a kernel launch onto threads, blocks, and a grid
Keep the programming model separate from the hardware warp

concepts.name: Kernel launch
concepts.summary: A host-side decision that creates millions of threads the hardware will schedule.

concepts.name: SIMT versus SIMD
concepts.summary: One instruction stream, many threads, with implicit lockstep and a way to mask lanes.
objectives: Explain why a scalar-looking kernel still runs in lockstep

concepts.name: Lanes and masks
concepts.summary: A disabled lane still occupies the cycle.

concepts.name: Warps and wavefronts
concepts.summary: The hardware scheduling quantum — 32 or 64 threads sharing an instruction.
objectives: Name the warp/wavefront as the unit the scheduler sees
Explain why block size that is not a multiple of the warp width wastes lanes

concepts.name: Execution resources
concepts.summary: ALUs, special-function units, and load/store pipes a SM/CU actually has.

concepts.name: GPU memory hierarchy
concepts.summary: Registers, shared/LDS, L1/L2, and HBM — different spaces, different costs.

concepts.name: Shared memory / LDS
concepts.summary: A software-managed scratchpad visible to a block.

concepts.name: Bank conflicts
concepts.summary: When several threads hit the same shared-memory bank and serialize.

concepts.name: Memory coalescing
concepts.summary: Adjacent threads touching adjacent addresses become one transaction.

concepts.name: Occupancy
concepts.summary: How many warps can live on a processor at once, limited by registers and shared memory.

concepts.name: Occupancy as a budget
concepts.summary: Registers × warps × blocks against a finite file.

concepts.name: Control divergence
concepts.summary: Threads in a warp taking different paths, so both sides run under a mask.

concepts.name: Latency hiding
concepts.summary: Switching to another ready warp instead of stalling the whole machine on a miss.

concepts.name: ILP versus TLP on a GPU
concepts.summary: Instruction slack inside a thread versus more warps.

concepts.name: Warp scheduling
concepts.summary: Which ready warp runs next, and why that interacts with caches and issue width.

concepts.name: Resource-limited launch
concepts.summary: Registers, shared memory, and warp slots as coupled constraints on a kernel.

concepts.name: Persistent threads
concepts.summary: A kernel that lives and pulls work, instead of one launch per tile.

concepts.name: Atomics and contention
concepts.summary: Read-modify-write that stays correct when many threads hit one address.

concepts.name: Unified virtual memory
concepts.summary: A single address space whose pages migrate, with a cost.

concepts.name: Tensor / matrix units
concepts.summary: Specialized pipes for dense matrix fragments.

concepts.name: Multi-GPU communication
concepts.summary: NVLink, PCIe, and the fact that 'the GPU' is often several.

concepts.name: Work graphs and capture
concepts.summary: Recording a launch sequence so the host is not in the inner loop.
